Database.// TablePrefix: Prepended to the framework's own 12 tables (FrameworkEntityTypes.All plus schema_migrations): users -> struo_users. Lower-case letters, digits and underscores, first character a letter, at most 16 characters; empty string = no prefix. Sample and fork tables are never prefixed. Changing it against a database that already holds framework tables makes startup create a fresh, empty set under the new names and seed them; rename the existing tables to match first. Override via env Database__TablePrefix.
Database.// MigrationsPath: Directory of reviewed *.sql migration scripts applied at startup, on ANY backend. Empty/absent = disabled (the default). Scripts here should only ALTER existing tables — creating tables is CodeFirst's job in every environment. See db/migrations/README.md.
Database.// AutoSyncSchema: DEV ONLY. true = CodeFirst structurally syncs EXISTING tables against the entities, which can MODIFY and DROP columns. Ignored (with a warning) outside Development. Creating missing tables happens regardless and is not controlled by this flag. Default false — see db/migrations/README.md for when auto-sync is unsafe.

Testing.// PostgresConnection: Opt-in PG integration suite (PostgresIntegrationTests). Set in appsettings.Development.json to a DISPOSABLE database whose name contains 'test'. Empty = tests skip. Env var STRUO_TEST_PG_CONNECTION overrides.

Struo.// ContentAssemblies: Assemblies scanned for [CmsCollection] content types. Add your content project's assembly name here (usually your content project's name), e.g. [ "Acme.Content" ]. The assembly must actually be resolvable via Assembly.Load, which means it must be registered in Struo.Api.deps.json (in practice, referenced by the host, e.g. via a ProjectReference) - a DLL merely sitting next to Struo.Api.dll is not enough - or the entry fails startup rather than being skipped.

Auth.// BootstrapAdmin: Seeded ONLY when the users table is first created. Ships a default admin/admin so a fresh install always has a login. OVERRIDE in production via env Auth__BootstrapAdmin__Email / Auth__BootstrapAdmin__Password (or appsettings.Production.json). A production start still on the default password logs a WARNING.
Auth.// Password: Plaintext password rules enforced at every write path (create user, change password). MinLength is also published to the SPA via GET /api/config for inline validation and generator length. MaxLength is a sanity bound only — Argon2id cost is fixed by its own parameters, not by input length. Override via env e.g. Auth__Password__MinLength=12 (read at startup; changing it requires a restart).

RateLimiting.// Login: App-layer, per-CLIENT-IP login rate limiter (POST /api/auth/login only). Enabled=false by default: admin-backend staff typically share one NAT egress IP, so per-IP partitioning collapses a whole office into one shared bucket, locking staff out of their own logins rather than stopping a distributed attacker — even with forwarded headers configured correctly. Set Enabled=true only for a single-instance, directly-reachable deployment with no edge/WAF in front of it whose users do not share an egress IP (a personal or single-tenant install, or a development host); if enabled behind a reverse proxy, UseForwardedHeaders with an explicit KnownProxies/KnownNetworks allowlist must be added first. RateLimiting:LoginAccount below is the layer that stays on by default. Override via env e.g. RateLimiting__Login__Enabled=true (read at startup; changing it requires a restart).
RateLimiting.// LoginAccount: App-layer, per-ACCOUNT login throttle (POST /api/auth/login only), backed by IDistributedCache and applied ahead of password verification. Counts FAILED attempts against the account being attempted (from the request body), regardless of source IP; a successful login resets the counter. Enabled=true by default — unlike RateLimiting:Login above, a per-account counter cannot collapse a shared-egress office into one bucket, since every account gets its own. Override via env e.g. RateLimiting__LoginAccount__PermitLimit=20 (read at startup; changing it requires a restart).
RateLimiting.// Password: App-layer change-password rate limiter (PUT /api/users/{id}/password only), partitioned by the authenticated user id rather than client IP. Enabled=true is secure-by-default; set false in multi-pod deployments where this in-memory per-pod limiter cannot enforce a global limit. The partition key is the ACTING user, not the target: a super-admin doing bulk resets spends down their own single bucket and gets throttled past PermitLimit, while every target's own budget is untouched — this also means the endpoint can never be used to lock a victim out of changing their own password. Raise PermitLimit here if the admin-side throttling becomes a problem. Override via env e.g. RateLimiting__Password__PermitLimit=20 (read at startup; changing it requires a restart).
